# SWIG bindings for libcosim — spike

**Status:** experimental spike, 2026-11-19.

- Round 1 (branch `spike/swig-bindings`): SWIG on the unmodified libcosim API.
- **Round 2** (branch `spike/swig-bindings-v2`, this version): the same
  bindings on top of `feature/binding-friendly-api`, which moves the
  adaptations that are also good C++ API into libcosim. See
  [Round 2](#round-2-on-top-of-the-binding-friendly-api) at the end.

**Goal:** check whether Python, C and (through C) Julia can all be generated by
SWIG from **one** shared interface.
See `proposals/language-bindings-facade.md` for the background.

## Result in short

| Language | Route | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Python | SWIG Python backend | ✅ 11/11 tests pass (`python/tests/test_spike.py`) |
| C | SWIG **experimental C backend** (SWIG 4.4.1) | ✅ smoke test passes, valgrind-clean (`c/smoke_test.c`) |
| Julia | plain `ccall` on the generated C library | ✅ smoke test passes (`julia/smoke_test.jl`) |

Covered in all three: loading an OSP config, the simulator name → index map,
model descriptions, `step` / `simulate_until`, last-value and time-series
observers (Python), file observer (Python), override manipulator, real-time
settings (Python), error mapping with `cosim::errc` codes, log level.

**Verdict:** "everything through SWIG" is feasible for Python, C and Julia.
The experimental C backend works, but it has sharp edges (below) that must be
handled once in the interface and documented for C users.

## Layout

```
bindings/swig/
  cosim.i               shared, language-independent interface (468 lines)
  python/cosim_python.i Python: time and path typemaps, CosimError (102 lines)
  c/cosim_c.i           C: time and path typemaps, catch-all exception handler (66 lines)
  python/tests/         Python tests (unittest, no extra dependencies)
  c/smoke_test.c        C11 program using only the generated header
  julia/smoke_test.jl   Julia ccall test against libcosim_c
```

Generated output: `libcosim/_cosim.so` + `cosim.py` (Python), `libcosim_c.so`
+ `cosim_c_wrap.h` (C, 234 functions).

## Building and running

SWIG comes from Conan (`swig/[>=4.4 <5]`) behind a new option, off by default:

```sh
conan install . -of build/spike -s build_type=Release -o "&:swig_bindings=True" --build=missing
B=build/spike/build/Release
source $B/generators/conanbuild.sh
cmake -S . -B $B -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$B/generators/conan_toolchain.cmake \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLIBCOSIM_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
      -DLIBCOSIM_BUILD_SWIG_BINDINGS=ON -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=$(which python3)
cmake --build $B -j

source $B/generators/conanrun.sh
PYTHONPATH=$B/bindings/python python3 bindings/swig/python/tests/test_spike.py
$B/output/release/bin/cosim_c_smoke tests/data/msmi/OspSystemStructure.xml
julia bindings/swig/julia/smoke_test.jl $B/output/release/lib/libcosim_c.so tests/data/msmi/OspSystemStructure.xml
```

## How much adaptation was needed

The libcosim headers were **not** modified. Every adaptation in `cosim.i` is
tagged, so it can be counted and later moved into libcosim (proposal §6):

| Tag | Count | Meaning | Move into libcosim? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[HIDE]` | 38 (74 `%ignore` lines in total) | hides extension-API or binding-hostile declarations | Mostly disappears with the user-API / extension-API header split (§6.6) |
| `[ADAPT]` | 14 | `%extend` / `%inline` replacing a hostile signature | Yes: these are the in-place overloads of §6.1–6.2 |
| `[GLUE]` | 3 | one-call loaders (`load_osp_config`, `load_ssp`) | Yes: §6.3 |
| `[REDECL]` | 2 | opaque base classes (`algorithm`, `observer`, `manipulator`, providers) | Disappears with the header split |

The `[ADAPT]` list matches the proposal's §6 predictions closely: time as
`double`, vector-returning getters instead of `gsl::span` out-parameters, a
result struct instead of three output spans, `std::optional` overloads,
`std::string` instead of `filesystem::path`, plain real-time getters and setters
instead of `std::atomic` structs, typed access to the `optional<variant>` start
value, and a log-level setter instead of inline Boost.Log.

## Findings

### General SWIG gotchas (all solved once in `cosim.i`)

1. **`%ignore` by name also hides `%extend` replacements with the same name**
   (including constructors). Hide by full signature, or ignore by name and
   re-enable the replacement by signature (`%rename("%s") ...(sig)`).
2. **`%extend` bodies and container `%template`s are processed where the class
   is declared.** Helpers, result structs and `%template`s must come *before*
   the `%include` of the class header, or conversions silently do not apply
   (a Python list was rejected as `std::vector<value_reference>`).
3. **`std::uint32_t` / `std::int64_t` are unknown to `stdint.i`**, which only
   declares the global names. Without `namespace std { typedef ::uint32_t
   uint32_t; ... }`, `value_reference` becomes an opaque type.
4. **`int64_t` width is platform-dependent:** SWIG must be told
   `-DSWIGWORDSIZE64` on Linux (where it is `long`), but not on Windows/macOS
   (`long long`). Handled in `CMakeLists.txt`. This will matter in CI.
5. **Default arguments:** ignoring the full signature does *not* hide the
   overloads SWIG generates for defaulted arguments. `compactdefaultargs`
   plus one replacement constructor per class avoids this.
6. **UseSWIG naming:** the Python module needs `OUTPUT_NAME cosim` (UseSWIG adds
   the `_`), and libcosim's global per-configuration output directories must
   be overridden for the module.

### SWIG experimental C backend

1. **No catch-all exception handling by default.** Without a `%exception`
   block, any libcosim exception calls `std::terminate` in the caller.
   Solved in `c/cosim_c.i`; errors become a pending `cosim_SWIG_CException`
   with `code` = `cosim::errc` value.
2. **Overloads are name-mangled from parameter types**, e.g.
   `cosim_fixed_step_algorithm_new_std_chrono_duration_Sl_cosim_detail_clock_rep_...`.
   Renaming does not help when hidden overloads had default arguments. Rule
   adopted: **no overloads in the C API**; constructors with variants become
   factory functions (`cosim_fixed_step_algorithm_create(step, threads)`),
   which matches libcosimc's existing naming.
3. **Upcasts are reinterpret casts.** Passing a `cosim_last_value_observer*` to
   `cosim_execution_add_observer(cosim_observer*)` reinterprets
   `shared_ptr<Derived>*` as `shared_ptr<Base>*`. This works for libcosim's
   single-inheritance hierarchy (valgrind-clean) but is formally undefined
   behaviour, and the manual states only single inheritance is supported. C
   callers must cast explicitly.
4. **Ownership is not visible in the header.** Functions returning objects
   return caller-owned handles (`*_delete`); member getters such as
   `cosim_model_description_variables_get` return *borrowed* pointers; string
   getters return a `strdup`ed `const char*` that the caller must `free()`.
   This needs documentation, or a naming convention enforced through `%newobject`.
5. **Parameter names are lost** (`carg1, carg2, ...`) in the generated header.
6. The backend is marked experimental (SWIG warning 524). The manual also
   lists "enums with a context like class or namespace are broken". libcosim's
   enums are namespace-level, and that worked here, but `-namespace cosim` is
   needed to prefix all C names.

### Julia

Plain `ccall` against `libcosim_c` works without any C++ toolchain coupling.
A real package would generate the `ccall` layer from `cosim_c_wrap.h` with
Clang.jl and add finalizers (ownership, finding C-4), a `check()` after each
call (exceptions), and `Dict` / `Vector` conversions. CxxWrap.jl is not needed
for this route.

### libcosim-side findings (candidates for in-place changes)

1. **Not all errors are `cosim::error`.** XML validation failures and missing
   SSD files throw plain `std::runtime_error` (no `errc` code), while a missing
   SSP archive throws `cosim::error` with code 8. Bindings can only give
   reliable error codes if libcosim is consistent.
2. **`variable_causality` and `variable_variability` are unscoped enums**, so
   bindings export bare names (`libcosim.input`, `libcosim.output`, ...). Make
   them `enum class` (like `variable_type`).
3. **Memory leak in OSP config parsing**, unrelated to the bindings: Xerces
   `DOMLSParser` / `DOMLSOutput` objects created in `osp_config_parser` and
   `extended_model_description` are never released (~960 bytes "definitely
   lost" per `load_osp_config` under valgrind).
4. **Verbose default logging:** libcosim logs at debug level by default, which
   floods script output. Bindings need a log-level setter from the start.

## Not covered by the spike

- Python packaging (wheels, stable ABI), Java and C#.
- Scenarios in memory, functions, `system_structure` builders, saved state.
- Callbacks from guest languages (user-written slaves and observers).
- `simulate_until_async` / non-blocking start.
- Windows and macOS builds (see gotcha 4).

## Suggested next steps

1. Move the `[ADAPT]` and `[GLUE]` items into libcosim as in-place changes, and
   split the headers into user API and extension API. Re-measure how much of
   `cosim.i` remains (expected: mostly typemaps and the C exception handler).
2. Fix the libcosim-side findings 1–3.
3. Add Java (SWIG) to confirm that the shared interface carries over to a third
   SWIG backend unchanged.
4. Generate the Julia layer with Clang.jl from `cosim_c_wrap.h`.
5. Register the three smoke tests with CTest and run them in CI on Linux and
   Windows.

## Round 2: on top of the binding-friendly API

Branch `feature/binding-friendly-api` (from `master`) contains, as separate
commits that can be cherry-picked:

| Commit | Change | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Fix Xerces memory leaks in OSP config parsing | libcosim-side finding 3 | fix |
| Throw cosim::error with error codes from config parsers | libcosim-side finding 1 | fix (non-breaking) |
| Make variable_causality and variable_variability scoped enums | libcosim-side finding 2 | fix (**breaking**) |
| Add plain-value real-time accessors to execution | replaces real-time `[ADAPT]`s | additive |
| Add vector-returning getters to last_value_observer | replaces getter `[ADAPT]`s | additive |
| Add sample-returning getters to time_series_observer | replaces sample `[ADAPT]`s | additive |
| Add one-call loaders for OSP and SSP executions | replaces all `[GLUE]` | additive |

The bindings were then switched to the native API, and `cosim::filesystem::path`
got a typemap per language (Python: `str` / `os.PathLike`; C: `const char*`),
which removed the remaining path adapters.

### Re-measurement

| | Round 1 | Round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `[ADAPT]` helpers in `cosim.i` | 13 | **7** |
| `[GLUE]` helpers | 2 loaders | **0** |
| `[HIDE]` tags / `%ignore` lines | 38 / 74 | 38 / 79 |
| `cosim.i` lines | 604 | **468** |
| language files (Python + C) | 122 | 168 |
| Python tests / C / Julia | pass / pass / pass | pass / pass / pass |
| valgrind, C smoke test, definitely lost | 960 B (Xerces) | **0 B** |

All seven additive/fix commits keep the existing C++ API working (except the
deliberate enum change), and the full libcosim test suite (35 tests) passes.

### What remains in `cosim.i`, and why

The 7 remaining adapters all wrap types that are idiomatic C++ but have no
natural C representation. They are reasonable to keep binding-side:

| Adapter | C++ type | Could move? |
|---|---|---|
| `execution::simulate_until(time_point)` | `std::optional<time_point>` | Only with an `optional` typemap family per language |
| `fixed_step_algorithm(step, threads = 0)` | `std::optional<unsigned>` | Same |
| `file_observer(logDir, configPath = "")` | two constructors, `std::optional<config>` | Same |
| `configured_execution::simulators()`, `has_end_time()` | `unordered_map`, `std::optional` | `std::map` would remove half |
| `time_series_samples::times_seconds()` | `std::vector<time_point>` | A container typemap per language |
| `variable_description::start_*()` | `std::optional<std::variant<...>>` | No; this is the right C++ type |
| `set_log_level(log_level)` | inline Boost.Log in `log/simple.hpp` | **Yes**: a Boost-free level setter in libcosim |

The C-only factory functions (`*_create`) for classes with several
constructors also remain, because the C backend cannot express overloads.

**The hide-list did not shrink**, as predicted: it consists of extension-API
methods (observer/algorithm/manipulator interfaces), lower-level functions
superseded by the new loaders, and the span-based overloads. It disappears
only with the user-API / extension-API header split (proposal §6.6), which
is the next decision point.

### New findings in round 2

1. **Member getters in C are borrowed, and it bites.** With the native
   `configured_execution` struct, `cosim_configured_execution_execution_get()`
   returns a pointer *into* the struct. Calling `cosim_execution_delete()` on it
   (correct for the round-1 helper, which returned a copy) caused a double free.
   The member is now `%immutable`, and the tests document the rule. A real C
   API needs one consistent ownership convention, e.g. only methods (owned
   results) and no public data members in the user API.
2. **Overloads hidden by signature do not cause C name-mangling** when they
   have no default arguments: `cosim_last_value_observer_get_real` and
   `cosim_scenario_manager_load_scenario` keep clean names although the C++
   methods are overloaded. Overloads *with* default arguments still do
   (round-1 finding C-2).
3. **C++20 `u8string()` returns `std::u8string`**: path typemaps need an
   explicit cast to `const char*` to compile under both C++17 and C++20.
4. The scoped-enum fix is visible in Python: `libcosim.input` became
   `libcosim.variable_causality_input`.
